ai-at-work.title: Bending Spoons to acquire productivity software startup Airtable for $1.285B
ai-at-work.excerpt: Technology holding company Bending Spoons S.p.A. today announced plans to acquire Airtable Inc., the developer of a popular cloud-based spreadsheet platform. The all-cash deal is worth $1.285 billion.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Bending Spoons is buying Airtable for 1.285 billion dollars in cash, which is actually less than what Airtable raised from investors and way less than its last valuation of 11.7 billion. This matters because Airtable's been a workplace staple for teams building custom workflows without code, so you're watching what happens when a hot productivity tool gets acquired by a company known for consolidating software assets. The valuation drop tells you everything you need to know about the current startup funding environment: yesterday's unicorn is today's acquisition target at a steep discount.

ai-at-work.title: AMD’s AI engine shifts into higher gear as data center revenue more than doubles and Helios ramps – but market is confused
ai-at-work.excerpt: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. delivered another strong quarter Tuesday, beating Wall Street expectations as its artificial intelligence infrastructure business continued its rapid expansion. The company
ai-at-work.dwp_take: AMD doubled its data center revenue year-over-year and is positioning itself as a serious competitor to Nvidia in AI infrastructure, though the market seems unsure what to make of it. This matters because the chips powering your workplace AI tools, search functions, and data processing are increasingly coming from AMD, which means your infrastructure teams need to understand this player's roadmap and reliability. Here's the thing: when Wall Street gets confused about good news, that's usually when smart enterprises quietly start testing alternatives to their single-vendor dependency.

ai-at-work.title: Open Secure AI Alliance proposes SAFE guidelines as membership tops 120
ai-at-work.excerpt: The Open Secure AI Alliance today proposed a set of guidelines for reporting cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence agents, one week after the group was formed. The proposal is call
ai-at-work.dwp_take: A brand new AI security alliance with over 120 members just dropped proposed guidelines for reporting cybersecurity incidents involving AI agents, called SAFE. This matters because AI is moving into production environments faster than most organizations can secure them, and having some shared standard for incident reporting could actually help us all learn from failures instead of pretending they didn't happen. The cynic in me notes that getting 120 companies to agree on anything is harder than herding cats, but at least someone's trying to build the guardrails before we really need them.

ai-at-work.title: DigitalOcean tops second quarter expectations amid surging AI demand
ai-at-work.excerpt: DigitalOcean Holdings Inc. today posted second quarter earnings that topped analyst expectations across the board. The company also raised its third quarter guidance. DigitalOcean launched in 2011 to
ai-at-work.dwp_take: DigitalOcean beat Q2 earnings expectations and raised forward guidance, riding a wave of AI infrastructure demand that's pushing developers toward simpler, cheaper cloud alternatives. For those of us building digital workplace infrastructure, this matters because it signals that teams are actively shopping around rather than defaulting to the big three clouds, which usually means more competitive pricing and better developer experience tools are actually moving the needle. Honestly, it's refreshing to see a company win by making things simpler instead of piling on features nobody asked for.

digital-culture.title: Emotional resilience is becoming the most valuable skill. Here’s why
digital-culture.excerpt: Global employee stress has reached a record high, according to Gallup’s State of the Global Workplace 2026 report. The report found that 44% of the world’s workforce reported significant daily stress.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Gallup's latest data shows global employee stress hitting record levels, with 44% of workers experiencing significant daily stress and emotional health metrics at decade-highs. For digital workplace professionals, this is a wake-up call that no amount of Slack channels or wellness app integrations will fix a broken culture. Here's the truth: you can have the slickest intranet and best collaboration tools on the planet, but if people are burned out and anxious, your digital workplace is just a fancy way to stress people out faster.

digital-culture.title: Your old role isn’t coming back
digital-culture.excerpt: Middle managers accounted for nearly a third of all layoffs in 2023, up from around 20% five years earlier. In 2024, Gartner predicted that through 2026, 20% of organizations would be using AI to flat
digital-culture.dwp_take: Middle management got hammered in 2023 and the trend is accelerating, with AI now becoming the official excuse to flatten org charts and eliminate roughly half of those roles by 2026. This matters because digital workplace professionals need to stop designing tools and processes assuming a traditional management layer exists to implement them. The irony is thick here: we built collaboration software to help managers coordinate teams, and now those managers are getting replaced by the very automation that software promised to enable.

industry-news.dwp_take: OnePlus is shutting down its North American Community platform on August 16, and users need to manually export their content before it vanishes. If your organization is betting everything on a third-party platform for internal collaboration, you might want to think about what happens when that vendor decides to pull the plug.

industry-news.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8 vs Motorola Razr Ultra: Which Is Right for You?
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Flip8 costs less and has longer support, while Motorola’s Razr Ultra leads on storage, RAM, battery, charging, and cover-screen apps. The post Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8 vs Motorola Raz
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung's latest flip phone is cheaper with better long-term support, while Motorola's model wins on raw specs like storage, RAM, and battery life. This matters because enterprises are finally taking foldables seriously for mobile work, and choosing between these two means deciding between total cost of ownership versus pure performance. Honestly, if your company is still debating whether foldables are a gimmick, you're already five years behind.

industry-news.title: Gmail’s New Feature Warns You Before Revealing You Were BCC’d
industry-news.excerpt: Gmail now warns BCC recipients before they reply all, helping prevent accidental exposure of their involvement and email address. The post Gmail’s New Feature Warns You Before Revealing You Were BCC’d
industry-news.dwp_take: Gmail is adding a warning that alerts people on the BCC line before they hit reply all, saving them from the classic mistake of accidentally exposing themselves to the whole thread. This matters because organizations have spent decades trying to educate employees about BCC etiquette, and most still don't get it, so having Gmail do the hand-holding is genuinely useful for compliance and keeping things confidential. Finally, technology is protecting people from their own instincts, which is probably the only way we were ever going to solve this problem.

industry-news.title: Apple Could Launch Camera-Equipped AirPods Before the End of 2026

industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is reportedly planning to release AirPods with built-in cameras by the end of 2026, which would let Siri see what users are looking at and understand their environment better. For digital workplace folks, this means AI assistants are about to get a lot more contextual and potentially more useful for hands-free work scenarios. Just what we needed: another device that can watch us while we're pretending to pay attention in Zoom meetings.
